papers.title: CAIR-MMOEA-DL: Contribution-Aware Inter-Robot Reallocation for Multimodal Multi-objective Multi-Robot Task Allocation
papers.abstract: Multi-robot task allocation (MRTA) is a fundamental problem in collaborative robot systems, where task allocation and route planning are tightly coupled. In static, offline MRTA problems, relying on a single assignment scheme can limit the flexibility of task allocation. Therefore, it is necessary to obtain high-quality Pareto front approximations and multiple alternative task allocation schemes. Although MMOEA-DL, a multimodal multi-objective evolutionary algorithm based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and large neighborhood search (LNS), addresses this problem effectively, some solutions may still suffer from workload imbalance, with a few robots becoming routing bottlenecks. To address this issue, this paper proposes Contribution-Aware Inter-Robot Reallocation MMOEA-DL (CAIR-MMOEA-DL). The method retains the bilevel structure of MMOEA-DL, where the upper level evolves task allocations and the lower level evaluates routes using a pretrained deep reinforcement learning planner. After the evolutionary search, a contribution-aware inter-robot reallocation strategy with coverage-guided target selection is applied to each solution on the first nondominated front of the final population. It identifies the robot with the longest route, ranks its tasks according to their removal contributions, and attempts to transfer selected tasks to lightly loaded or positive-coverage target robots. Large neighborhood search is then used to refine the task-visiting order. Experiments on 16 simulated MRTA instances with 10 independent runs show that CAIR-MMOEA-DL significantly improves hypervolume (HV) and Pareto-set proximity (PSP) compared with four baseline algorithms. Ablation results further show that the performance gains are accompanied by additional post-search assignment evaluations and longer computation time.

papers.title: State-Based Reinforcement Learning Safe Trajectory Tracking for Autonomous Vehicles via Geometric Safety Representation and Lagrangian-PPO
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a state-based safe trajectory tracking (STT) control framework for autonomous vehicles in dynamic environments, where the objective is to design a controller that ensures accurate trajectory tracking while guaranteeing non-conservative collision avoidance. Existing learning-based approaches often suffer from inaccurate geometric safety representations and unstable training when incorporating safety constraints. To address these challenges, we propose a geometry-aware framework by integrating an analytical rotating supporting hyperplane (RSH)-based safety representation with a Lagrangian Proximal Policy Optimization (Lagrangian-PPO) reinforcement learning algorithm. By modeling vehicles and obstacles as rigid ellipsoids, an explicitly differentiable signed distance is derived to provide a continuous and non-conservative safety cost. Based on this representation, the trajectory tracking problem is formulated as a constrained Markov decision process, enabling unified optimization of tracking performance and safety via a reward–cost decoupled learning structure. Finally, asymptotic convergence and effectiveness of the proposed approach are validated through simulation and Vehicle-in-the-Loop (ViL) experiments, demonstrating superior tracking accuracy and robust obstacle avoidance compared with existing methods.

papers.title: Tiltrotor Tricopter Dynamics and Control Using the Gibbs–Appell Formulation and Integrated Feedback Linearization with LQR-PD Control
papers.abstract: The equations of motion of a flying robot composed of n rigid arms, each equipped with a motor at its end to provide controllability during complex three-dimensional maneuvers, were previously derived in [1]. The most significant outcome of that study was the demonstration that the robot can reach any point in space while simultaneously achieving an arbitrary desired orientation. It was shown that accomplishing this objective requires at least six actuators and, consequently, six propellers. However, increasing the number of actuators results in higher manufacturing costs, greater energy consumption, and increased overall weight. Therefore, the development and analysis of more efficient flying robot configurations become increasingly important. In the design proposed in this paper, a three-arm flying base is employed instead of a six-arm configuration, with a propeller mounted at the end of each arm. A distinctive feature of this design is that each propeller, in addition to rotating about its primary axis, can also rotate about a secondary axis. This capability enables the thrust vector generated by the main propeller motor to be reoriented by means of a smaller auxiliary motor, thereby allowing the robot to achieve arbitrary orientations in space. To facilitate the analysis, the flying robot is decomposed into several open-chain robotic structures. The equations of motion of the individual chains are first derived using the Gibbs–Appell formulation and then combined, while accounting for the constraints governing the interactions among the chains, to obtain the dynamic model of the complete system. Finally, the capability of the proposed tiltrotor tricopter to perform complex three-dimensional maneuvers is evaluated through an integrated feedback-linearization and LQR–PD control framework.

papers.title: RIS-on-UAV-Assisted MC-DCSK Communications Under Mobility: System Modeling and Performance Analysis
papers.abstract: This paper investigates RIS-on-UAV-assisted multi-carrier differential chaos shift keying (MC-DCSK) communications under mobility. A ground control station (GCS) transmits an MC-DCSK signal to a moving unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), where an onboard reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) assists the receiving process. The considered architecture is motivated by reliable reception for mobile UAV links. The GCS-to-UAV channel is modeled as a multipath fading channel, while the discrete-time receiver explicitly preserves the path delays in the sampled reference and data-bearing branches. The received signal consists of a direct branch and an RIS-assisted branch, where the RIS contribution is incorporated as an additional coherent gain without introducing a separate RIS-to-UAV propagation channel. UAV mobility is captured through a Doppler-induced timing error model. Based on the discrete-time correlator output, the mean and variance of the decision variable are derived under the Gaussian approximation, and the corresponding bit-error-rate (BER) expression is obtained. Numerical results show that increasing the RIS size significantly improves the BER performance, whereas higher UAV velocity degrades performance due to more severe timing mismatch. The impacts of the number of channel paths, the RIS size, the UAV velocity, and the spreading factor are also quantified. These results indicate that RIS-on-UAV-assisted MC-DCSK is a promising framework for reliable UAV communications under mobility.

papers.title: An Efficient Hierarchical Planning Framework for UAV Navigation in Narrow Dynamic Tunnel
papers.abstract: Ground robots are common in tunnels, yet rugged terrain and limited space make UAVs superior due to their agility. However, traditional hierarchical planning methods suffer from low global search efficiency, prolonged local re-planning times, and limited capability for diverse dynamic obstacles. To address these issues, this paper proposes the CG-ST Planner, which integrates coneguided global planning with spatio-temporal detection local re-planning. We design a cone-guided A* algorithm that mitigates the inefficiency of traditional A* by constraining the search space. To avoid dynamic obstacles efficiently, we introduce an event-triggering mechanism based on a moving cylindrical detection area. The UAV focuses solely on this forward region rather than the entire map, significantly reducing the computational burden. Finally, a local window re-planning algorithm ensures rapid responsiveness for obstacle avoidance. Simulation results in various tunnel scenarios demonstrate that our framework improves global planning efficiency by up to 98.57% and reduces local re-planning time by over 90% compared to traditional A* and TEB algorithms. Crucially, in dynamic environments with diverse obstacle trajectories, it maintains a greater safety distance while successfully completing the avoidance task in all simulated scenarios. These findings validate that the CG-ST Planner offers a promising solution for UAV path planning in constrained and dynamic environments.

papers.title: AI-Based Personalized Travel Planning and Recommendation System: A Unified Framework for Intelligent Trip Planning
papers.abstract: A growing number of travel planning activities involve managing multiple pieces of often competing data about destinations, budget, weather, attractions' availability, transportation options and personal preferences that are typically distributed across a number of isolated online services. Traditional travel-planning tools tackle these issues one at a time: choosing or navigating, and rarely include personalization, predictive analytics, and multi-constraint reasoning within a single interface. We propose a unified framework for personalized travel planning that integrates personal preferences, context-based destination recommendation, budget- and weather- aware filtering, and route and distance analysis, and AI-assisted itinerary generation. The framework is inspired, and to some extent generalized, from the design of the ongoing academic research prototype TripCraft, an AI-powered agent for trip planning. We build upon the state of the art of recommender-systems theory, context-aware recommendation, tourist trip design (route optimization) literature, and recent large language model-based agents for travel-planning to develop a system-level description, a hybrid AI/ML approach, and a step-by-step algorithmic process for creating personalized itineraries that take preference, budget, weather and route constraints into account. We provide preliminary proof of concept based on a synthetic evaluation on fabricated records using baseline comparisons and constraint-compliance metrics. The findings are only indicative of the possible effectiveness, but do not constitute proof of concept. The expected contribution is the conceptual and methodological foundation for unifying preference-, budget-, weather- and route awareness in intelligent travel planning.

papers.title: The Shift from Google Search to ChatGPT: How Generative AI Is Changing Students’ Information-Seeking Behaviour
papers.abstract: The rapid spread of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT is changing how students search for, understand, and verify academic information, a role long held by search engines such as Google. This study examines students’ self-reported information-seeking behaviour with Google Search and ChatGPT, covering frequency of use, purpose, first-source preference, reasons for adoption, trust, verification practice, and perceived change. A descriptive, quantitative survey was conducted using a 25-item structured Google Forms questionnaire administered to college and university students through convenience sampling (N = 200). Data were analysed using frequency and percentage analysis. Of the respondents, 73.5% use ChatGPT/AI at least once a day, and 61.2% name ChatGPT/AI as their first source for academic answers, compared with 30.6% for Google Search. Understanding concepts, faster answers, and easier explanations were the main reasons for use. Trust was conditional: 59.2% verify ChatGPT answers always or often, 59.2% have encountered incorrect or misleading output at least sometimes, and Google Search was the most common verification source (42.9%). In total, 93.9% reported at least some change in how they find information. The findings point to a hybrid, AI-assisted pattern rather than a replacement of search engines; however, they rest on self-reported data from a non-probability sample and cannot be generalised.
